text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said there would be no compromise over national interests during forthcoming foreign secretary talks with India.
- The European Union is to impose an anti-dumping fine of 14.2 per cent on Pakistan's exports of unbleached cotton fabric, down from an initial decision to impose 25 percent duty.
- Seven people, including five policemen and a small girl, were shot dead when a police van was ambushed in Larkana town.
- Twenty-four countries have so far confirmed their participation in the OIC summit to be held in Islamabad.
- Three people, including a child, were killed when a gunman fired on a mosque near the town of Faisalabad.
- Torrential rain hit northern and southern Pakistan in the last 24 hours. More rain and thunderstorms are expected in the next 24 hours.
- Money supply grew 3.66 percent and domestic credit 11.56 percent in July-December, while foreign assets of the banking system declined by 77.4 billion rupees.
- The IMF has expressed concern at cuts in the public sector development programme and a meagre 40 percent disbursement of funds in the first eight months of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).
- The government has fixed July 1, 1998 as the deadline for deregulation of prices petroleum product prices,
- The government might announce a package of incentives to recover loans from defaulters.
- Trade liberalisation with India top the agenda of foreign secretary-level talks between India and Pakistan.
